core_obligations: Reduce to an affine reduced base: by locality on the base of flatness and finite presentation assume S = Spec(A) with A reduced, note that a finite type morphism is quasi-compact so X is quasi-compact, and cover X by finitely many affine opens X_i = Spec(B_i) with B_i a finite type A-algebra and F restricted to X_i the sheaf associated to a finite B_i-module M_i (proof lines 5262-5280).

Record the transition data: for each pair i, j choose an ideal I_ij of B_i cutting out the complement of X_i cap X_j, set M_ij = B_i/I_ij and observe that M_ij is a finite B_i-module whose support is V(I_ij) (proof lines 5280-5285).

Apply the algebraic generic flatness input to the pairs (A to B_i, M_ij) and (A to B_i, M_i) to obtain dense opens, and intersect them all into one open dense U of S built as a finite intersection (proof lines 5287-5300).

Verify the claim at a point u of U: take the localizations witnessing the good properties of the finitely many pairs, multiply the chosen elements into a single f with u in D(f), and after base changing to A_f read off that X over S is quasi-compact, locally of finite presentation and flat and that F is flat over S and of finite presentation over O_X (proof lines 5302-5336).

Finish the finite presentation bookkeeping: because each M_ij is of finite presentation over B_i, the intersections X_i cap X_j are quasi-compact open in X_i, which the author converts into quasi-separatedness of X over S using the same-chapter characterisation (proof lines 5337-5343).
proof_roadmap: Work affine locally on a reduced base and cover X by finitely many affines with finite modules, including the transition modules M_ij attached to the pairwise intersections (proof lines 5262-5285).

Apply the reduced-form algebra input to all pairs at once, intersect the resulting dense opens, localise at a chosen point, and read off flatness and finite presentation of X and F over the localised base (proof lines 5287-5343).
difficulty_reason: The proposition is the reduced-base form of generic flatness: for a finite type morphism f : X to S with S reduced and a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf F on X there is an open dense U of S over which X is flat and of finite presentation and F is flat over U and of finite presentation over O_X (statement lines 5246-5260). The counted proof has a real assembly layer of its own on top of the algebra input: it makes the base affine and reduced, covers X by finitely many affines with finite modules, introduces one auxiliary finite module M_ij for each pair of chart intersections so that those intersections can be controlled, intersects the finitely many dense opens produced by the algebra input, and then localises once more at a chosen point to read off the four flatness and finite presentation statements together with quasi-separatedness of X over S (proof lines 5262-5343). It is H2: the deep flatness input is the cited algebra lemma, while the contribution of this argument is the geometric assembly, which is carried out in the counted span and is not a citation.
